## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 49 (*Jivhānicchāraka*) is a training rule from the *Vinaya Piṭaka* governing decorum during eating, translated by Bhikkhu Brahmali as "Sticking out the tongue". It forms part of the sekhiya section regulating personal deportment, specifically proscribing monastics from sticking out their tongue while eating.
